title: Benjamin Libet's neural timing studies
summary: Eric Wargo tells of Benjamin Libet's neural timing studies, about 1970s-1980s at unspecified, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: this is the the Benjamin libbit work back in the 70s and 80s his those landmark studies that he did

plain: Eric Wargo, a writer on precognitive dreams and synchronicities, points on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels to the work of Benjamin Libet, a scientist who ran what Wargo calls landmark studies in the 1970s and 80s on the timing of activity in the brain. Wargo uses them to support his ideas about how the mind relates to time, which, if true, would help explain how people might sense the future.
